_about: Card seeds for the existing Factory (Director -> Worker -> Checker) to rebuild itself as the constitutional institutions. Each seed is a unit of intent with an acceptance contract, not an implementation plan: the Director splits seeds into Factory cards after the Fit Report (C0.00). Seeds may be split, never merged, dropped or widened without an approved delta in AR-13. Thresholds marked [PROPOSED] are design proposals for Isa to ratify in AR-13, not evidence. [PLACEHOLDER] values are resolved only by the open item named in open_items.

phases.name: Protect and measure
phases.intent: Protect governance, add trustworthy memory, and measure today's Director -> Worker -> Checker Factory so the simulation can be validated against it. No change to how work is allocated.
exit: C0.13 backcast result recorded, pass or fail
Isa approves the phase exit through the interim gate (C0.02)

phases.name: Rules, Market, Court and Scaler
phases.intent: Run the pull rules, licences and elastic capacity in the Ledger; stand up the Work Market and Assurance Court beside Director -> Worker -> Checker, then cut over with a rollback path.
entry: AR-08 and AR-10 signed before the cards that name them start
exit: Isa approves the phase exit through the interim gate (C0.02)

phases.name: Audit, Release Gate and live operation
phases.intent: Mark the markers, gate every change including governance, and give live operation an owner.
exit: Protected governance paths now pass the Release Gate and Isa (C2.02 replaces the interim gate)

phases.name: Inquiry, Council and Planning
phases.intent: Replace the Director's planning with the three deliberative institutions. Low volume lets them start semi-manually under their charters.
exit: Release Gate promotion of the phase

phases.name: Trial and decision
phases.intent: Run the trial against pre-registered predictions and criteria, then decide go or no-go.
entry: AR-12b signed: trial dates and scope, set after admission from the measured baseline

cards.title: Fit Report: map the pack onto the existing Factory
cards.intent: The pack was written without access to the Factory's code. Before any other card is created, the Director reads the codebase and reports, card by card, what exists, what must change and what conflicts.
scope: For each card seed: the components it touches, classified KEEP / UPLIFT / REPLACE / NEW (the parked design's classification in docs/design-parked/constitutional-factory-design-notes.md §18 is the starting hypothesis, not a finding)

Answer the parked coupling questions: how many call sites choose a model; does any code rewrite history rows; where workflow state lives; can adapters report usage and throttling; are tests separable from implementation paths; how the Factory changes its own governance code today
Today's roster of models, their access routes and today's predetermined mapping (R11 start state)
Where the Owner's hashed keys live and how adapters obtain usable credentials (OI-04)
Proposed deltas: seeds to split, and any seed whose premise does not hold, with evidence
acceptance: Every card seed in the pack appears in the report with a classification and the files or modules it touches
Every open item marked 'Fit Report' in open_items has an answer or an explicit 'not determinable from code' with the reason
No seed is dropped, merged or widened in the report; changes appear only as proposed deltas for AR-13
The report cites file paths and commit for every claim about the codebase
evidence: Fit Report document stored with the pack's manifest hash

cards.title: Register this pack as a versioned, hash-verified record
cards.intent: The pack is the constitution's first ratified input. Store it so every later card can cite the exact version it was built from.
scope: Store factory-pack.json and manifest.json; verify every sha256 in the manifest
Record the ratification (AR-13) as a human-authored record
Record the mapping from pack card IDs to Factory card IDs as cards are created
acceptance: pack/test_pack.py passes on the stored copy
A changed byte in any stored pack file is detected by hash check
Every Factory card created from the pack carries its pack card ID and the pack version

cards.title: Protected governance paths, with an interim gate
cards.intent: No change approves itself. Before the Factory edits its own rules, the files that hold the constitution, charters, Ledger rules, Scaler and burn-cap settings, and this pack are protected.
scope: Define the protected path list (AR-11)
Block any merge touching a protected path unless it carries an approval record from Isa and a pass from a checker other than the change's author
Interim gate until C2.02: Director -> Worker -> Checker's Checker plus Isa's approval record
Alert on any attempted change to a protected path
acceptance: A test change to a protected path without an approval record is blocked
The same change with an approval record and an independent pass merges
The author of a change cannot supply its own approval
The protected path list is itself protected
evidence: Blocked and allowed test merges recorded

cards.title: Append-only Ledger beside today's operational state
cards.intent: Memory is governed, and facts and claims are kept apart. Add an append-only, replayable Ledger alongside the existing SQLite state without disturbing running work.
scope: Append-only event log with a hash chain
Facts (tool output, git state, usage, timings), claims (model assertions) and derived values (rule outputs) in separate tables
Operational state rebuildable from the Ledger (projections)
SQL as canonical operational state; Git as the artifact authority (DQ9)
The parked schema docs/design-parked/ledger-schema.sql is a reference: its assignment, draw and shadow-price tables are superseded by pull (R1) and must not be built
acceptance: UPDATE and DELETE on Ledger tables abort
Rebuilding projections from the Ledger reproduces the live projection exactly
Director -> Worker -> Checker keeps running unchanged while the Ledger is written in shadow
Any recorded rule decision can be recomputed from the Ledger (replay)
evidence: Tests for append-only enforcement and replay

cards.title: Adapters record usage for every model invocation
cards.intent: Token use, cost and throttling are the inputs to the Scaler, the burn cap and calibration. Record them as facts from the adapter, never as model claims.
scope: Per invocation: provider, model ID and version, reasoning effort, input, cached-input and output tokens, list-price cost, latency, throttle or error codes
Keyed to idea, card, value-stream step and attempt
acceptance: Every model invocation in a sample week has a usage record
Recorded cost reconciles with the vendor's invoice or usage console within [PROPOSED] 2%
Throttle events (for example HTTP 429) are recorded with the rate-limit headers the vendor returns

cards.title: Key custody: no secret in the Ledger, a fingerprint for attribution
cards.intent: The Owner holds the vendor accounts and keys; they are hashed in the Factory. The Ledger may record which key was used, never the key.
scope: Adapters obtain credentials from the Owner's store as the Factory does today (Fit Report)
The Ledger records a key fingerprint (hash) per vendor account and invocation
Secret scanning of the Ledger, logs, prompts and the pack
acceptance: A secret scan of the Ledger, logs and repository finds no key material
Rotating a key changes its fingerprint and does not break usage attribution
A model invocation cannot be made with a key the Owner has not registered

cards.title: Record every value-stream step for today's Factory
cards.intent: Measure today's Factory on the same steps the simulation uses, so the two can be compared.
scope: Map Director -> Worker -> Checker stages onto the value-stream steps: discover, challenge, human intent ratification, design, plan, plan check, human plan ratification, build, review, security review, merge and CI, audit, acceptance test, release, deploy, live operation (docs/idea/value-stream.md §2)
Per card and idea: start, end, waiting time and outcome at each step; rework and its cause
Steps today's Factory does not perform are recorded as absent, not inferred
acceptance: The stage-to-step mapping is written down and ratified by Isa
For a sample week, every idea and card has a complete step timeline or an explicit 'absent step' record
Lead time, change-failure rate and step hours can be computed by SQL query alone

cards.title: Record dependencies and the artifact versions each card read
cards.intent: R17 needs to know what each card depends on and which version of its prerequisites it built against. X13 needs the Factory's real coupling.
scope: Dependencies between requirements and between cards, as planned
The artifact versions (commits) each card read when built
Stale rebuilds: cards redone because a prerequisite changed
acceptance: For a sample week, coupling (share of dependent requirement pairs) and stale rebuilds per idea can be computed by SQL query
Every card's read versions are recorded at build time

cards.title: Record defect provenance and which families missed it
cards.intent: Blind spots shared by every model family are the one failure no organisation fixes. Measure them, and every check's catch rate.
scope: For every defect found anywhere, including live: where it was introduced, which check caught it, which checks passed it, and the model family behind each check
Deterministic evidence (tests, CI, typed contracts) recorded as first-class evidence (DQ10)
acceptance: For a sample week, the catch rate of each check and the share of escaped defects missed by every family that checked them are computable by SQL query

cards.title: Idea value ledger: cost to artifact, and return after ratification
cards.intent: An idea is worth nothing without action. Measure what it cost to turn an idea into an artifact, then from ratification to production and any monetisation or real-world return.
scope: Segment 1: idea intake to first artifact (merged code or ratified document): model spend and recorded human hours
Segment 2: ratification, production and return events, with the value the Owner records
Ideas with no action are recorded as 'no action', value zero
acceptance: For every idea, segment 1 cost is computable from Ledger facts alone
The Owner can record a ratification, production or return event against an idea
A report lists ideas by segment 1 cost and, where recorded, return
evidence: Value report for a sample period

cards.title: Package the simulation twin and reproduce the recorded results
cards.intent: The value-stream simulation is the hypothesis. Make it runnable inside the Factory, pinned to the pack's commit, with its parameters read from a file.
scope: probes/value-stream/vs_sim.py and the modules it imports (probes/institutions/factory_sim.py, probes/portfolio6/select6.py), pinned by the hashes in manifest.json
Every assumed parameter listed in the pack's twin_parameters read from one parameter file
Output the same measures as live (M01-M05, M11-M13)
acceptance: python3 -m unittest discover -s probes/value-stream passes inside the Factory
With the default parameter file, the institutions with the six reproduce 24.9 clean ideas a week (claim CL-01)
Changing a parameter in the file changes the run; no parameter is hard-coded outside it

cards.title: Baseline: measure today's Factory for the shadow period
cards.intent: Replace assumed volumes with measured ones. This is the data the trial is sized from and the twin is calibrated on.
scope: Run C0.04-C0.09 for the shadow period [PLACEHOLDER: length, set in AR-12a]
Report the demand profile, token use per card and step, pass rates per model, step and tier, coupling, catch rates, change-failure rate, lead times, cost per idea to artifact, human attention hours
acceptance: Every measure M01-M18 has a value for the period, or a recorded reason it cannot be measured under Director -> Worker -> Checker
Variance per measure is reported (needed for AR-08 standards)

cards.title: Calibrate the twin on the baseline
cards.intent: Fit the simulation's assumed parameters to what the Factory actually does.
scope: For each twin parameter: fitted value from the baseline, or 'not measurable yet' with the assumption kept
Sensitivity: which unmeasured parameters move the predictions most
acceptance: Every parameter in twin_parameters is marked fitted (with the measure and period used) or assumed (with the reason)
The calibrated parameter file is stored as a versioned record

cards.title: Backcast: does the twin reproduce today's Factory?
cards.intent: Before its predictions for the institutions are trusted, the calibrated twin must reproduce the Factory it was calibrated on.
scope: Run the twin as Director -> Worker -> Checker with the calibrated parameters and today's roster
Compare with the baseline on clean ideas, change-failure rate and cost per clean idea
acceptance: Result recorded against X9's criterion: each of the three measures within 25% of the baseline, or a fail
On a fail, the causes are listed and the model is revised before C0.14; the revision is a new record, not an overwrite

cards.title: Pre-register predictions for the trial
cards.intent: Criteria fixed before data. Record what the twin predicts for the trial configuration before the trial runs.
scope: Run the calibrated twin for the trial configuration in AR-12a
Record predicted ranges for M01, M03, M04, M05, M12 as a sealed record
The uncalibrated predictions in this pack (predictions section) are the prior; the calibrated run replaces them
acceptance: Predictions are stored before the trial starts and cannot be changed afterwards
Each prediction names the parameter file and code version that produced it

cards.title: Weekly report: live against the model
cards.intent: One weekly view that compares the Factory with its own predictions, built on SQL views, no new tool.
scope: SQL views for every measure M01-M20
Weekly comparison with the sealed predictions (C0.14) once they exist
Isa's attention hours shown every week
acceptance: The report is generated from Ledger queries alone
Each figure links to the query that produced it

cards.title: Card schema: tier, requirements, dependencies, interfaces, contract
cards.intent: Cards must carry what the rules read.
scope: Absolute work tier (1-3, H5)
Requirement links; dependencies; the interfaces between requirements named in the plan (DQ11)
Acceptance contract hash, including locked tests
Value-stream step; author and the author's model family
One requirement per build invocation until X12 measures otherwise
acceptance: A card without a tier, requirement link or contract is rejected at creation
Card versions are immutable; a change creates a new version

cards.title: Tier-setting rules in Planning
cards.intent: Card difficulty is set by rules over card facts, never by a model's judgement, and corrected by escalation.
scope: Tier from card facts: size, files, risk paths, dependencies (Idea Record §2)
Which card facts set the tier, per institution (DQ1)
acceptance: The same card facts always give the same tier (replay)
The rule set is a protected path

cards.title: API access for the seven-model menu, under the data rule
cards.intent: Staff the menu on API tokens, with no tier that trains on our data, and read real rate limits.
scope: Adapters for the menu in the pack's menu section, through the routes AR-10 approves
A route is registered only with a recorded no-training confirmation for that tier (R15); Muse Spark's Contributor tier is excluded
Vendor rate limits recorded as Scaler caps (replacing the assumed 8 per model, 48 in all)
A second route where AR-10 names one (for example OpenRouter for Muse Spark)
acceptance: Registering a route without a no-training confirmation fails
Each menu model answers a test invocation and its usage is recorded (C0.04)
Each route's rate limit is stored as a fact with its source

cards.title: Shadow replay: menu models on historical cards
cards.intent: Estimate each menu model's pass chance per step and tier on this Factory's own work before it takes live cards. This replaces the estimated benchmark scores.
scope: Replay a sample of accepted historical cards [PLACEHOLDER: sample, set in AR-12a] on each menu model
Mark results with the same checks the cards passed
Record pass rates, cost and time per model, step and tier
acceptance: Every menu model has a recorded pass rate per step and tier on the sample, with its size
The estimated Coding Index values (marked * in the menu) are replaced by measured pass rates for licensing

cards.title: Licences and pull: hardest first, oldest first
cards.intent: Nobody assigns work. An agent with a free slot pulls the oldest card in the highest tier it is licensed for, and sees its own record when it pulls.
scope: R1 pull; R2 licence ladder; R3 hardest first, oldest first, no choice within a tier
R10: at pull time the agent sees its licences, recent rate against the standard and its recent markdown reasons; it may decline without a markdown; repeated declines return the licence
R11 start state: today's predetermined mapping; the start for menu models not in today's mapping per OI-12
The Ledger views each agent sees at pull time (DQ5)
acceptance: An agent cannot pull a card above its licence
Within a tier, the pulled card is always the oldest
An agent's pull view contains only its own record
Every pull is replayable from the Ledger

cards.title: The ladder: promotion, two-speed demotion, fast track
cards.intent: Success and velocity push an agent up to the hardest tier it can sustain; failure moves it down.
scope: R5 as written, with the constants set once in the constitution (pack: constitution.constants)
Quality standards per institution and tier from AR-08
A minimum sample per tier before velocity comparisons count (RK4)
acceptance: Promotion credit +1 per accepted card at home tier, -4 per markdown; stretch cards compulsory at the credit threshold
Promotion after 20 trial cards meeting the tier's quality standard
Gross demotion (over 2x the standard) after 10 cards; marginal (over 1.25x) only after two consecutive failing batches of 20
A failed promotion doubles the credit needed next time, capped at 2x; a new model needs 5 credit until its first failed promotion
Every licence change cites the rule and the counts that caused it
evidence: Rule tests against the pull-rules simulation's scenarios (probes/pull-rules)

cards.title: Hard-work reserve for capped agents (dormant under API tokens)
cards.intent: R7 protects a subscription cap for hard work. The menu runs on API tokens, so no seat is capped today; the rule must exist for any subscription seat P8 admits.
scope: R7 as written, applied only to agents with a subscription cap
Uncapped agents unaffected
acceptance: With no capped agent, the rule changes no decision (test)
With a simulated capped agent, it spends below its home tier only the capacity above what its home tier needs at 75% of full speed until reset

cards.title: Attribution with evidenced reason codes
cards.intent: Every markdown lands on the producer that caused it.
scope: R8 reason codes and the evidence each requires (DQ3)
Implementation to implementer; unclear or wrong card to its author in Planning; review miss found later to the reviewer and the implementer; infrastructure to nobody
acceptance: A markdown without a reason code and evidence is rejected
Card-caused markdowns are counted against the card's author, not the builder

cards.title: Markers are marked; late marks count double
cards.intent: Marking is accountable in both directions, and escaped defects cost more.
scope: R9: a pass later overturned by Audit, or a markdown overturned as unfounded, counts against the reviewer under R5
R12: an Audit finding weeks later applies like an immediate markdown, counted twice
acceptance: An overturned pass changes the reviewer's record
A late Audit finding is weighted twice in the producer's record

cards.title: No orphan tiers, with recorded waivers; escalation optional
cards.intent: Small teams deadlock without R13. Keep work moving and record every relaxation.
scope: R13: cards waiting at a tier with no licensed agent past a set time give the best agent one tier below stretch cards; if none, split in Planning or escalate to Isa
R13 may relax licences, independence and seat rules, each with a Ledger record (Idea Record §5.3)
R6 escalation is optional (§3.2): build it switchable, default per AR-13
acceptance: No card waits beyond the R13 limit without a waiver or escalation record
Every waiver names the rule relaxed, the card and the reason
evidence: Deadlock tests with one-model and two-model rosters

cards.title: Family independence
cards.intent: No model reviews, audits or releases work by a model of its own family.
scope: R18: family = vendor; instances and siblings are one epistemic source
If no other family is available, the waiver is recorded (R13)
acceptance: A same-family review, audit or release is refused unless a waiver record exists
Instances of one model count as one model

cards.title: High-impact licence floors
cards.intent: The steps where a mistake costs most need the most reliable models, chosen by evidence.
scope: R19: design, plan, plan red-team, security review, acceptance test and release need a pass chance of at least 0.8; other steps 0.6; review 0.5
Pass chance from the same evidence as every licence (C1.04, then live records)
acceptance: A model below a step's floor cannot take that step
When a model's record changes, its eligibility re-sorts without manual change

cards.title: Evidence-gated dependencies
cards.intent: Build only on reviewed work.
scope: R17: each card reviewed as built; no whole-idea barrier
A dependent card becomes available only when its prerequisite has passed review
A rework invalidates only the dependants whose inputs changed
The Ledger records the artifact versions each card read (C0.07)
acceptance: A dependent card is not pullable before its prerequisite passes review
After a rework, exactly the dependants that read the changed version are invalidated
No waiting limit converts to building on unreviewed work (the hybrid was tested and loses)

cards.title: The Scaler: elastic instances started and stopped by rule
cards.intent: Agents are instances of menu models, started and stopped by Ledger arithmetic, not by an agent.
scope: R14 as written (pack: parameters PR-01 to PR-09)
Price every queued task on every licensed model clearing the 0.8 floor: $/busy hour x hours / pass chance; cheapest wins
Target = busy instances + ceil(queued hours / drain target); held cards count as demand; clamp to vendor rate limits (C1.03)
Start the shortfall; stop instances idle 30 minutes beyond target
Cost-band pull at 1.5x unless the task has waited an hour
Instances of one model are one model for independence
acceptance: Every start and stop cites the counts and rule that caused it, and replays
No instance takes a task below the floor or outside the cost band before the wait expires
Rate limits read from C1.03 are never exceeded
evidence: Rule tests; replay; comparison with the twin's Scaler on the same queue

cards.title: Burn cap and monthly ceiling
cards.intent: Spend follows demand, within limits Isa sets.
scope: R16: running instances burn at most 2x the trailing seven-day average ($/hour)
Monthly ceiling = expected demand x cost per clean idea x 1.5; initial value from AR-05, reset from measured volume (C0.11)
When the cap binds, trim the most expensive model first
acceptance: Simulated overspend is trimmed before the cap is exceeded
The ceiling and cap are protected paths
Isa is notified when the monthly ceiling is [PROPOSED] 80% spent

cards.title: Rolling portfolio policy
cards.intent: The menu changes on evidence, never by chasing the leaderboard.
scope: P1 two top-tier models from two vendors, repaired at once
P2 no vendor above half the seats
P6 new models earn seats on evidence: one trial seat at a time; replaces the weakest incumbent only if its Ledger value per dollar beats it by 10%
P7 never chase the leaderboard
P8 match the help-down rule to how the seat is paid; top seats on API tokens
acceptance: A menu with fewer than two top-tier vendors triggers a repair record at once
A new model enters only through a trial seat with a recorded comparison

cards.title: Assurance Court
cards.intent: Is this work acceptable? Decided blind, deterministic checks first.
scope: Reviewers blind to author; open standing to challenge with evidence; other verdicts visible only after committing one's own
Deterministic checks first: build, tests, static analysis, CI, typed contracts (DQ10)
A reproduced defect beats any number of approvals
acceptance: A review cannot see the author's identity or reasoning
A failing deterministic check blocks acceptance whatever the model reviews say
A reproduced defect overturns prior approvals

cards.title: Cut-over: Work Market and Court replace Worker and Checker, with rollback
cards.intent: Move execution and checking to the institutions while the Director keeps planning, with a tested way back.
scope: Shadow the Market and Court on live cards before switching [PLACEHOLDER: shadow length, set in AR-12a]
Switch Workers to pull and the Checker to the Court
Rollback to Director -> Worker -> Checker by configuration, tested
acceptance: Rollback restores Director -> Worker -> Checker without data loss (tested)
During shadow, Market and Court decisions are recorded beside the live ones for comparison (X1)

cards.title: Audit
cards.intent: Is assurance trustworthy? Auditors outside the work's provenance chain mark the markers.
scope: Random plus risk-weighted samples (the model used 10%)
Planted defects with known answers, which also test the auditors
Isa's sample
Findings feed R9 and R12 (C1.09)
acceptance: No auditor audits work in its own provenance chain or family
Planted defects are recorded with their catch or miss

cards.title: Release Gate
cards.intent: Is an accepted change safe to run inside the Factory? Criteria fixed before data.
scope: Approvers from different families, blind, with one seated dissenter; cooling-off period; no version approves itself
Canary results against criteria fixed in advance
Acceptance test (QA) of the whole idea and release approval (value-stream steps 11-12)
Takes over protected governance paths from the interim gate (C0.02): rule changes pass the Release Gate and Isa
acceptance: A change cannot be approved by a version of itself
Release criteria are recorded before canary data exists
A protected-path change now requires the Release Gate and Isa

cards.title: Live operation: incident, restore, hotfix
cards.intent: The value stream continues past the Release Gate. Give live operation an owner.
scope: Incident detection, restore and hotfix cards (value-stream step 13)
The owner decided in AR-09a (the value-stream document gives one example: the Release Gate owns rollback, the Work Market takes hotfix cards, the Ledger marks change-failure rate and restore time)
acceptance: Every incident has an owner, a restore time and, where needed, a hotfix card
Change-failure rate and restore time are recorded as evidence against the releasing change

cards.title: Configurations as trial proposals
cards.intent: Step affinities found by search are trials, never the constitution.
scope: R20: the Ledger may propose step affinities from its own records as a trial configuration
Compared with the institutions on the same work; adopted only on evidence
Lapses automatically when the roster changes or a reserved pool is empty
acceptance: A configuration without a recorded comparison cannot be adopted
Removing a model from a reserved pool ends the configuration automatically

cards.title: Inquiry
cards.intent: Independent discovery: commit before seeing any other submission.
scope: Participants on the same brief, committing before any peer output is visible
Sizing: the institutional model found two analysts sufficient (Idea Record §5.3); X7 tests universal participation. The trial compares both
acceptance: No participant sees a peer output or identity before committing
evidence: Manifest audit of what each participant saw

cards.title: Deliberation Council
cards.intent: Shared understanding without prestige or dominance.
scope: Anonymous labels; random reading order; no chair; no vote
Every proposition appears in the synthesis; one objection keeps a point disputed
One round (Idea Record §5.3)
Output: the Alignment Record for Isa's ratification, with minority positions
acceptance: No identity is visible to Council participants
Every Inquiry proposition is traceable in the synthesis

cards.title: Planning Chamber replaces the Director's planning
cards.intent: Intent to executable cards: blind parallel decomposition, then reconciliation and a separate red team.
scope: Decomposers blind in parallel; reconciler; red team separate from the reconciler
One planner plus a red team (Idea Record §5.3)
Plans name the interfaces between requirements (DQ11)
Tier-setting rules (C1.02)
acceptance: Planning sees the Alignment Record, including minority positions, never the Council transcript
Every card traces to a requirement in the Alignment Record

cards.title: Ratification tiers and Isa's attention budget
cards.intent: Human ratification is the likely real ceiling. Route to Isa only what the rules say needs her.
scope: Which ideas need Isa's ratification and which the Council may ratify (AR-09b)
A weekly attention budget with alerts when it is exceeded
Isa's fixed touchpoints: standards, Alignment Records, amendments, governance changes at the Release Gate, R13 escalations
acceptance: Every ratification request cites the rule that routed it to Isa
Weekly attention hours are reported (M17)

cards.title: Trial plan: dates and scope
cards.intent: Set the trial's dates and scope once the cards are in the backlog and the baseline is measured.
scope: Start date and duration from the backlog forecast
Scope from the measured demand profile (C0.11), not the assumed 25 ideas a week
Which phases the trial covers
acceptance: AR-12b signed by Isa

cards.title: Run the trial and judge X1-X14
cards.intent: Each experiment can prove the idea wrong. Judge each against its pre-registered criterion.
scope: Weekly live-against-prediction report (C0.15)
Each experiment X1-X14 judged against its falsification criterion in the pack
X9 on the sealed predictions (C0.14)
acceptance: Every experiment has a recorded verdict (not falsified / falsified / not testable yet, with reason)

cards.title: Go / no-go, and retiring the old roles
cards.intent: Isa decides on the evidence. Go retires Director -> Worker -> Checker; no-go rolls back.
scope: Decision record against AR-12a's success and kill criteria
On go: retire the Director, Worker and Checker roles through the Release Gate
On no-go: roll back (C1.18) and record why
acceptance: Isa's decision recorded with the evidence it cites
Either the old roles are retired through the Release Gate or the rollback is complete
